correctness.rationale: For p>=13 the degree-twelve polynomial is squarefree precisely off A=+/-2, giving genus five. The exact coefficient extraction of (z^2+Az+1)^((p-1)/2) makes the 5x5 Cartier matrix diagonal or antidiagonal, with reciprocal paired entries. The finite-characteristic Legendre generating series gives each scalar coefficient as (-1)^d P_d(A/2). On each 1- or 2-cycle of the inverse-Frobenius-semilinear Cartier map, nonzero coefficients imply stable bijectivity, and zero coefficients force a zero cycle. Thus p-rank is precisely the weighted indicator formula (2,2,1). Legendre polynomial degrees are d<= (p-1)/2 with nonzero leading coefficient; the second-order Legendre ODE and nonvanishing P_d(+/-1) prove simple roots strictly within the smooth locus. The exact determinant factor and divisor multiplicities follow. The included stdlib verifier separately checks polynomial identities, rank/stable rank, squarefreeness and sample gcds in all 44 primes 5<=p<200; this does not substitute for the all-prime proof.

originality.rationale: Ohashi--Kudo arXiv:2603.21569v1 Section 4.3 equation (4.13), Proposition 4.9, Proposition 4.11 and Algorithm 3 already provide the family, a decomposition into elliptic factors and tests for superspeciality. The final claim is not that decomposition nor superspeciality: it is the explicit all-parameter p-rank formula and a factorization of its determinant into three separable Legendre polynomials whose geometric roots and multiplicities are individually determined for every prime. Source text and claim-level searches found no stated equivalent or dominating geometric rank-drop divisor theorem. A generalized Legendre-form result and standard elliptic isogeny reasoning remain priority risks, explicitly acknowledged. This is a qualified best-knowledge originality assessment, not a claim that no older deduction exists.

value.rationale: A natural one-dimensional moduli subfamily of genus-five hyperelliptic curves with large automorphism groups was introduced for superspeciality. Its complete ordinary/nonordinary p-rank profile is a motivated invariant beyond the zero-rank slice; the three separable divisors and their exact characteristic-dependent degrees and determinant multiplicities quantify every individual rank-drop mechanism. The p=13 and p=19 cases illustrate different geometric intersection patterns. This is not an arbitrary numerical instance or finite table recomputation, and the theorem holds for all primes in scope. The full Newton polygon and universal intersection census remain open.
